context:
Goal: merge ready PRs without a second full CI run.
Problem (rule): every merge to main makes each ready PR's records page stale, so each one must go back to draft, get a page-only push, a new draft run, ready again and a new ready run, while main moves again; it needs your word because it changes how the merge tool treats a reviewed head.
Based on (ruling): your pick on the earlier records-page question (15:02 CST Nov 14, option c: skip CI on a records-only push after a green head), built in PR #3349 (merged 2026-11-14), and decision records-index-at-merge: a ready PR with a stale records page goes back to draft.
Based on (read): runner 10's report via the coordinator, 14:19 CST Nov 16 (relayed; triage read no run); the same refusal hit #3583 at 12:36 CST. Runner 10 expects it on #2817 and #3553 too.
Departs from: main — decision records-index-at-merge sends a ready PR with a stale records page back to draft; option a has the merge tool write the page itself on a ready head.
Meanwhile: no merge, flag or override is requested; the three PRs wait, and triage keeps its other work.
holds: Ready pull requests #3577, #2817 and #3553, and every ready PR after each merge, cannot merge until the records page is fresh.

options.gain: Ready PRs merge in one step even while main keeps moving.
options.how: On a ready head, the merge tool writes the records page as a page-only commit and merges, with no second full CI run, since a page-only commit changes no code.
options.label: The merge tool refreshes the records page itself on a ready head
options.lose: The merge tool adds a commit to a head that was reviewed; the length of a ready run is unmeasured, so the time saved is unknown.

options.gain: The head that merges is exactly the head that was reviewed and run.
options.how: A ready PR with a stale page goes back to draft, gets the page-only push (your earlier pick skips its CI), then is marked ready again.
options.label: Keep the round trip: back to draft, page-only push, ready again
options.lose: Each merge to main sends every ready PR through the trip again, and a PR can lose the race while main moves.

ref: runner 10's finding at 14:19 CST Nov 16, relayed by the coordinator: #3577's merge was refused at 14:18 CST on a green, clean, ready head (records page stale); same as #3583 at 12:36 CST

shown.label: The merge tool refreshes the records page itself on a ready head
Keep the round trip: back to draft, page-only push, ready again

title: When main moves, should the merge tool refresh a ready PR's records page itself, or should the PR go back to draft each time?
why: The coordinator recommends a and has not measured the ready-run length; triage read no diff and agrees only on the cost shown: a stops the trip that repeats after every merge. It is a recommendation, not owner-typed.
